**Finding submitted: `needs_review` (confidence 0.72), no redline proposed.**

**Why not a deviation/missing insert:**

The TRANSITION rule's own detection guidance scopes the insert trigger to services/hosting agreements. This document isn't one — it's the APCN 2 submarine cable construction & maintenance agreement, a multiparty consortium instrument in which Teleglobe USA Inc. is a co-owning Party, not a customer buying hosted services. There is no vendor, no defined "Customer Data," and no counterparty holding our data in custody.

**Exit mechanics that do exist** (handled on a consortium rather than vendor-exit model):
- §18.4 (p0231) — remaining Parties must negotiate a reasonable agreement to ensure continuous operation of a terminating Terminal Party's station; the functional analogue of transition assistance
- §18.5 (p0232) — reallocation of the terminating Party's interests and obligations
- §18.6 (p0234) — one-year asset realization plus an obligation to execute transfer documents
- §18.7 / §32.6 (p0235, p0280) — accrued liabilities survive
- §31.4 (p0274) — confidentiality tail of five years post-termination

**The directional point that drove the call.** Data return in machine-readable format and certified deletion are genuinely absent. I deliberately did not insert them, because the model language is Vendor-facing and this agreement is symmetric: every Party would be bound, including us. We are ourselves a record-keeper under §9 and §10, and a deletion covenant would cut directly against the retention and audit rights we hold under §9.8 and the five-year confidentiality tail. Firing the standard insert here would have manufactured an obligation on our own client while dressing it up as a protection — so I flagged rather than redlined.

**What a human should confirm:** whether anyone treats the Network Administrator or Central Billing Party (Annexes 3 and 4) as holding Teleglobe operational or billing data custodially. If so, the right fix is a narrow, mutual copy-out right on exit in §18, negotiated at consortium level — not a unilateral vendor-exit clause.
